cr_data.provenance: (Alfred Stieglitz, New York, NY); Jacob Strand, New York, NY, 1925; Paul Strand, New York, NY, date unknown; The New Gallery, New York, NY, 1950; Private collection, New York, NY, 1950; Parke-Bernet Galleries, Inc., New York, NY, sale no. 1344, lot no. 55, 7 May 1952; Private collection, New York, NY, 1952; Sotheby Parke Bernet, Inc., New York, NY, sale no. 3057, lot no. 79, 21 May 1970; The artist, 1970; Estate of the artist, 1986; Private collection, 1987; (Greenberg Van Doren Gallery, St. Louis, Missouri); (Kurt Borné Gallery, Kansas City, Missouri) (Source: Lynes, 1999)
remarks_1999: Whitney Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks indicate, "Exam. at Mr. Strand's house, Feb. 1946. . . . No signature. Three calla lilies. Owned Mr. Jacob Strand. Anderson Gals, Stieglitz 7 American, 1925. Bought by Jack Strand." 1970 auction entry indicates, "On the reverse is an oil study of a red gladiolus" [not verified]. Titled *Lilies* by Stieglitz on Abiquiú Notebooks photograph. Reproduced in *International Studio* (May 1925). (Source: Lynes, 1999)

titles.notes: Source of title: Whitney Archive, Downtown Gallery Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks, 1925 New York (Anderson) exhibition checklist.
titles.title: Calla Lilies

description: Three white calla lilies, clustered together, dominate the composition. A bright yellow spike protrudes from the center of each. Three green stems are visible beneath the blooms. The white and gray background resembles layers of draped, light-colored fabric.
title: Calla Lilies
